items.question: A main engine cylinder liner shows signs of cold corrosion. The scavenging air temperature is correct, but the cylinder oil feed rate is at the minimum recommended level. What is the most appropriate technical action for a 2nd Engineer to take?
options: Increase the cylinder oil feed rate and consider using a lubricant with a higher Base Number (BN).
Decrease the jacket water cooling temperature to reduce thermal stress on the liner.
Increase the fuel injection pressure to ensure more complete combustion.
Reduce the scavenging air pressure to increase the dew point temperature.
items.explanation: Cold corrosion occurs when the liner temperature falls below the dew point of sulphuric acid. Using a higher BN oil neutralizes the acid, and increasing the feed rate provides a better protective film.
items.regulation: MAN B&W Service Letter / Wartsila Technical Bulletin on Cold Corrosion

items.question: Under MARPOL Annex VI, what is the maximum allowable sulfur content for fuel oil used by a ship operating outside of a designated Emission Control Area (ECA) as of January 1, 2020?
items.explanation: The global sulfur cap was reduced from 3.50% to 0.50% effective 1 January 2020 under Regulation 14 of MARPOL Annex VI.

items.question: A ship is equipped with a 15 ppm bilge water separator. If the oil content meter (OCM) fails while the vessel is in a Special Area, what action should the 2nd Engineer take regarding bilge discharge?
options: Stop all overboard discharge of bilge water immediately.
Continue discharge but monitor the overboard water visually.
Bypass the OCM and rely on the separator's efficiency.
Discharge only during daylight hours to ensure visibility.
items.explanation: MARPOL Annex I requires a functional oil filtering equipment and an automatic stopping device (OCM). If the monitoring equipment is faulty, discharge must cease.

items.question: When managing a major engine overhaul, the Chief Engineer identifies that the budget for spare parts will be exceeded. What is the most appropriate leadership action?
options: Postpone the overhaul until the next fiscal quarter to save costs.
Use non-genuine spare parts to stay within the original budget.
Provide a technical justification and risk assessment to the technical manager for additional funds.
Instruct the 2nd Engineer to reuse old gaskets and seals to save money.
items.explanation: Management-level officers must balance safety, maintenance requirements, and budgeting by communicating technical needs through proper channels using risk assessment.
items.regulation: ISM Code Part A, Section 3 (Company Responsibility and Authority)

items.question: Which parameter is the most critical to monitor on a centrifugal pump to prevent cavitation when the suction tank level is low?
options: Net Positive Suction Head Available (NPSHa)
Motor current (Amperes)
Discharge valve position
Pump shaft RPM
items.explanation: Cavitation occurs when NPSHa drops below the NPSH required (NPSHr). Monitoring suction pressure and tank levels is critical to prevent pump damage.
items.regulation: General Marine Engineering Practice / Manufacturer Guidelines

items.question: A Blackout occurs due to a 'Reverse Power' trip on the lead generator. What is the most likely cause of this trip?
options: The prime mover of the generator failed or lost power.
The generator suffered a short circuit in the windings.
The busbar frequency was too high.
The voltage regulator failed to increase the excitation.
items.explanation: A reverse power trip occurs when the generator stops producing power and instead begins to draw power from the busbar, acting as a motor, usually because the prime mover failed.

items.question: According to STCW, what is the minimum rest period required for an engineer officer in any 7-day period?
options: 70 hours
77 hours
84 hours
96 hours
items.explanation: STCW requires that the hours of rest shall be not less than 10 hours in any 24-hour period and 77 hours in any 7-day period.

items.question: During a scavenge space inspection, the 2nd Engineer finds heavy carbon deposits and 'lacquering' on the liner walls. What is the most likely operational cause?
options: Excessive cylinder oil lubrication or low load operation.
High fuel injection temperature.
Low scavenging air pressure.
Leaking exhaust valves.
items.explanation: Heavy carbon and lacquering are typical results of unburned cylinder oil or fuel residues, often associated with low load operation where temperatures are insufficient for complete combustion.
items.regulation: MAN B&W Operation Manual / Marine Engineering Practice

items.question: When planning the maintenance of the main air compressors, the Chief Engineer notes that the vessel will be in a high-traffic zone for 48 hours. What is the best scheduling decision?
options: Proceed with the maintenance as per the PMS schedule regardless of location.
Delay the maintenance until the vessel is in open sea to ensure full air availability for maneuvering.
Perform the maintenance on both compressors simultaneously to finish faster.
Ask the deck department to reduce speed so one compressor is sufficient.
items.explanation: Safe navigation is the priority. Maintenance that reduces redundancy in critical systems (like starting air) should be deferred until the vessel is not in a high-risk maneuvering area.

items.question: A crosshead-type main engine is operating with high scavenge air temperature. After cleaning the air cooler, the temperature remains high and the pressure drop across the cooler is normal. Which of the following is the most likely cause?
options: Fouling on the water-side of the air cooler tubes
Leaking exhaust valves
Blocked turbocharger inlet filters
Worn piston rings causing blow-by
items.explanation: If the air-side pressure drop is normal, the air-side is clean. High outlet temperature despite a clean air-side suggests poor heat transfer from the cooling medium, typically caused by scale or bio-fouling on the internal water-side of the tubes.

items.question: Under MARPOL Annex VI, Regulation 13, what is the required action when a major component of a marine diesel engine is replaced with a non-identical component or an additional component is installed?
options: The engine must be re-certified to demonstrate compliance with the applicable NOx emission limits
The EIAPP certificate must be discarded and a new IAPP requested immediately
No action is required if the engine power increases by less than 15%
The change must be recorded in the Engine Logbook without notifying the Administration
items.explanation: A 'substantial modification' as defined by the NOx Technical Code includes the replacement of a component with a non-identical part that affects NOx emissions, requiring re-certification.

items.question: According to the ISM Code, if a piece of machinery identified as 'critical' fails, what is the immediate requirement for the engineering management?
options: Follow the specific contingency plans and report the non-conformity to the DPA
Delay the report until the machinery is repaired to show proactive management
Transfer the responsibility of the repair to the shore-based technical team only
Continue operations as normal if a standby unit is available without reporting
items.explanation: The ISM Code requires that the safety management system identifies critical equipment and provides for specific measures (contingency plans/reporting) in the event of failure to ensure continued safety.

items.question: While paralleling two alternators, the incoming machine's frequency is slightly higher than the busbar frequency. The breaker is closed when the synchroscope pointer is at the '11 o'clock' position moving slowly clockwise. What will be the result?
options: The incoming machine will take a small amount of load and remain stable
The incoming machine will experience a reverse power trip
A severe mechanical shock will occur due to phase opposition
The busbar voltage will drop to zero momentarily
items.explanation: Closing the breaker just before '12 o'clock' (synchronism) while moving clockwise (incoming machine faster) ensures the machine picks up load (kW) rather than drawing it, which is the correct procedure.

items.question: When developing a dry-docking budget, which cost category is typically the most difficult to predict and represents the highest financial risk?
options: Unforeseen 'open and inspect' findings (e.g., tailshaft wear or steel replacement)
Standard paint and grit blasting costs
Daily dry-docking fees (dock rent)
Service engineer attendance for scheduled overhauls
items.explanation: While fixed items are easily budgeted, the 'growth of work' resulting from inspections of components that cannot be seen while the ship is afloat (steel thickness, rudder/shaft clearances) represents the highest budgetary risk.

items.question: A main engine fuel pump for a cam-less (Electronic) engine is showing erratic injection pressure. The 'FIVA' (Fuel Injection Valve Actuator) or proportional valve is suspected. What is the first diagnostic step?
options: Check the electrical signal/feedback and clean the pilot valve filters
Manually override the valve with a hammer to loosen the spool
Replace the entire fuel pump assembly immediately
Increase the booster pump pressure to bypass the actuator
items.explanation: Electronic engines rely on fine filtration and precise electrical signals. The FIVA valves are sensitive to debris in their pilot oil supply; checking filters and signal integrity is the standard first response.
items.regulation: Manufacturer Guidance (MAN B&W ME-C / WinGD RT-Flex)

items.question: A centrifugal pump is vibrating excessively after a bearing replacement. The shaft was checked for run-out and is within limits. What is the next logical step in troubleshooting?
options: Check the alignment between the pump and the motor
Replace the impeller as it must be out of balance
Tighten the gland packing until the vibration stops
Operate the pump at a higher RPM to pass the resonance point
items.explanation: After reassembly, misalignment between the driver (motor) and the driven unit (pump) is the most common cause of vibration, even if individual components are balanced and shafts are straight.

items.question: When managing a multicultural engine room team, a Chief Engineer notices that a junior officer never asks questions despite making repetitive minor errors. How should this be addressed?
options: Implement a 'closed-loop communication' policy and encourage 'tool-box talks' to foster psychological safety
Issue a formal warning for incompetence to the junior officer
Assign the junior officer to clean the bilges as a corrective measure
Assume the officer understands and wait for a major error to intervene
items.explanation: Effective leadership (HELM) involves recognizing cultural power distances and using structured communication tools (like closed-loop and TBTs) to ensure understanding and reduce the fear of asking for help.
items.regulation: STCW Section A-III/2 (Leadership and Managerial Skills)

items.question: Which document is required to be maintained on board to record the transfer of fuel oil between tanks for a ship of 400 GT and above?
options: Oil Record Book, Part I
Oil Record Book, Part II
Ship Construction File
Bunker Manifold Transfer Log
items.explanation: Oil Record Book Part I (Machinery Space Operations) is mandatory for recording internal transfers of fuel oil, bunkering, and bilge water management.

items.question: According to MARPOL Annex VI, what is the maximum permissible sulfur content for fuel oil used on board a ship operating outside an Emission Control Area (ECA) since January 1, 2020?
items.explanation: Effective from 1 January 2020, the global sulfur cap for fuel oil used on board ships outside ECAs is 0.50% m/m.

items.question: During a bunkering operation, the Bunker Delivery Note (BDN) must be kept on board for how long, and where must the representative fuel sample be stored?
options: BDN for 3 years; sample in a safe location until the fuel is substantially consumed but not less than 12 months.
BDN for 1 year; sample in the laboratory for the duration of the voyage.
BDN for 5 years; sample in the engine room until the next bunkering.
BDN for 2 years; sample in the Chief Engineer's office until the vessel reaches a drydock.
items.explanation: MARPOL Annex VI requires the BDN to be kept for 3 years and the representative sample to be retained for at least 12 months.

items.question: A Chief Engineer is planning the annual budget. A major overhaul of the turbocharger is due, but the company asks to postpone it to the next fiscal year. How should the Chief Engineer justify the maintenance now?
options: Inform the company that the 2nd Engineer is too busy to do it later.
Perform a risk assessment showing the impact on fuel efficiency, EEDI/CII ratings, and the potential for catastrophic failure.
Increase the spare parts order for other machinery to hide the turbocharger costs.
Agree to postpone but document that the company took the decision against his advice in the logbook.
items.explanation: Technical leadership requires data-driven decision making. Highlighting regulatory compliance (CII) and safety risks (catastrophic failure) provides a professional justification for necessary expenditure.
items.regulation: ISM Code Part A, Section 10 (Maintenance of the Ship and Equipment)

items.question: Which parameter change indicates a deteriorating condition of a plate-type central cooler (fresh water/sea water)?
options: Decrease in pressure drop across the sea water side.
Increase in the temperature difference (delta T) between sea water inlet and outlet with constant heat load.
Decrease in the approach temperature (difference between FW outlet and SW inlet).
Increase in pressure drop across both sides with a corresponding decrease in cooling efficiency.
items.explanation: Fouling in plate heat exchangers typically results in higher flow resistance (increased pressure drop) and reduced heat transfer coefficient (lower efficiency).

items.question: During the inspection of a large 2-stroke engine, you find 'cold corrosion' on the upper cylinder liners. What is the most likely cause?
options: Operating the engine with the cylinder oil feed rate set too high.
Operating the engine at low loads with the liner wall temperature below the dew point of sulfuric acid.
High vanadium content in the fuel oil.
Using cylinder oil with a Base Number (BN) that is too high for the fuel's sulfur content.
items.explanation: Cold corrosion occurs when the cylinder liner temperature falls below the dew point of the sulfuric acid generated during combustion, common in slow-steaming scenarios.
items.regulation: CIMAC Guide to Marine Fuel Management

items.question: A 2nd Engineer reports that the Planned Maintenance System (PMS) is showing multiple overdue items because the vessel has been in heavy weather. How should the Chief Engineer handle this?
options: Instruct the 2nd Engineer to mark them as 'completed' to avoid negative vetting reports.
Prioritize safety-critical equipment, document the reasons for delay in the PMS/Logbook, and inform the Technical Superintendent.
Stop all other work and force the crew to work overtime until the PMS is clear.
Delete the overdue tasks and reschedule them for the next month.
items.explanation: The ISM Code requires maintenance to be carried out and documented. If delays occur due to operational safety (weather), the correct procedure is risk-based prioritization and transparent reporting.

items.question: When paralleling two AC generators, which condition must be met before closing the circuit breaker of the incoming machine?
options: The incoming machine must be at a slightly lower frequency than the busbar.
The voltages must be equal, and the synchroscope must be rotating slowly in the 'Fast' direction, passing the 11 o'clock position.
The phase sequence must be reversed to ensure torque balance.
The incoming machine load must be set to 50% before closing the breaker.
items.explanation: Synchronizing requires equal voltage, same frequency (slightly higher on incoming), and phase coincidence to ensure the incoming machine takes load rather than becoming a motor.

items.question: A main engine fuel pump high-pressure pipe bursts and the fuel oil leaks onto a hot exhaust manifold, starting a fire. The local fixed water-mist system activates automatically. What is the Chief Engineer's primary concern regarding the engine's operation?
options: The cost of the water consumed by the system.
Thermal shock to the engine components and potential water ingress into the intake.
Checking if the oil record book is up to date during the fire.
Restarting the engine immediately to maintain steerage.
items.explanation: While extinguishing the fire is priority, technical management involves understanding that localized cooling from water-mist can cause thermal cracking of hot castings or engine seizure if water enters the induction system.

items.question: During a bunkering operation, the bunker delivery note (BDN) density differs significantly from the lab analysis of the previous batch. How should the Chief Engineer adjust the centrifugal purifiers?
options: Adjust the gravity disc size or the interface set point based on the new density to ensure the water-oil interface is correctly positioned.
Increase the throughput to ensure faster processing of the heavier fuel.
Decrease the heater temperature to prevent vaporization of lighter fractions.
Disable the water transducer to prevent false sludge discharge alarms.
items.explanation: The efficiency of a purifier depends on the correct placement of the interface. Density changes require a corresponding change in gravity discs (manual) or automated set-points to prevent oil loss or water carryover.
items.regulation: Alfa Laval / Westfalia Separation Manuals; ISO 8217

items.question: A major crankcase explosion is preceded by high oil mist detector (OMD) alarms. After the engine has stopped, what is the most critical safety action?
options: Do not open any crankcase doors for at least 20-30 minutes to prevent the ingress of fresh air.
Immediately open the crankcase doors to allow the explosive gases to vent.
Spray water on the crankcase doors to cool the internal hot spot.
Restart the lube oil pump to cool the affected bearing.
items.explanation: Opening doors introduces oxygen to a fuel-rich atmosphere containing a hot spot, which can trigger a secondary, more violent explosion. Cooling time is essential.
items.regulation: IACS M10: Protection of internal combustion engines against crankcase explosions

items.question: Under the ISM Code, how should a Chief Engineer handle a recurring failure of a 'critical' piece of machinery that the current PMS fails to prevent?
options: Raise a Non-Conformity (NCR) or Technical Deficiency report to the DPA and request a revision of the PMS intervals.
Increase the frequency of overhauls locally without informing the office to keep the vessel running.
Ignore the failure if it does not lead to a total blackout.
Delegate the repair to the junior engineers and record it as a routine task.
items.explanation: The ISM Code requires the reporting of non-conformities and the analysis of causes to prevent recurrence. A failure in the PMS system itself must be addressed through the Company's safety management system.

items.question: What is the primary purpose of the 'break-in' period when installing new piston rings in a large two-stroke diesel engine?
options: To allow the rings and liner to achieve a compatible surface finish through controlled wear.
To ensure the lube oil pump reaches maximum pressure.
To allow the cylinder head bolts to stretch to their final tension.
To burn off the preservative grease applied by the manufacturer.
items.explanation: Running-in or breaking-in is the process where the peaks of the surface asperities are worn down in a controlled manner to create a seal and permit effective lubrication.
items.regulation: STCW Code Table A-III/2 (Marine Engineering at Management Level)

items.question: The engine room is filling with smoke, and a fire is confirmed near the fuel purifiers. As 2nd Engineer, the Chief Engineer is not immediately reachable. What is your first priority?
options: Sound the fire alarm, ensure the safety of personnel, and initiate the emergency shutdown of fuel pumps and fans.
Try to extinguish the fire alone with a portable CO2 extinguisher before raising the alarm.
Immediately activate the fixed CO2 system for the entire engine room.
Wait for the Chief Engineer to arrive before taking any action to avoid mistakes.
items.explanation: Standard emergency response dictates: Alarm, Personnel Safety/Accounting, and Isolation (stopping fuel and air) to prevent fire spread.

items.situation: The Chief Engineer notices that the vessel's oily water separator (OWS) 15ppm alarm is frequently flickering, and the Second Engineer suggests bypassing the alarm sensor 'just for this watch' to finish pumping the bilge holding tank before arrival. The tank is nearly full.
items.question: What do you do? Explain your actions in order.
key_steps: Reject the suggestion immediately and reinforce MARPOL compliance requirements.
Stop all bilge discharge operations until the equipment is verified.
Troubleshoot the OWS sensor, checking for fouled glass or oil carryover.
Ensure all oily water is retained on board in holding tanks if the OWS is unreliable.
Log the maintenance and any equipment malfunction in the Oil Record Book Part I.
items.critical_step: Prohibit any bypass of the 15ppm monitoring system to prevent illegal discharge.
items.regulation: MARPOL Annex I, Regulation 14 (Oil filtering equipment)

items.situation: During a routine inspection of the steering gear room while at sea, the Second Engineer discovers a major hydraulic leak on one of the rams. The pressure is dropping, and the rudder response is sluggish. The vessel is in a narrow channel with moderate traffic.
items.question: What do you do? Explain your actions in order.
key_steps: Alert the bridge immediately and advise the Master of the steering limitation
Switch to the redundant hydraulic pump/system and isolate the leaking unit
Engage emergency steering procedures if the bridge loses control
Replenish the hydraulic oil reservoir to maintain system pressure
Begin immediate repairs only after the vessel is in a safe position or at anchor
items.critical_step: Alert the bridge immediately and advise the Master of the steering limitation

items.situation: While bunkering in port, the bunker manifold pressure suddenly spikes, and a gasket on the vessel's manifold fails, spraying fuel oil onto the deck and into the water. The bunker barge is still pumping at a high rate.
items.question: What do you do? Explain your actions in order.
key_steps: Signal the bunker barge to execute an Emergency Stop immediately
Close the vessel's manifold valve and the tank filling valves
Initiate the SOPEP (Shipboard Oil Pollution Emergency Plan) and mobilize the response team
Plug the scuppers (if not already done) and use absorbents to contain the deck spill
Report the spill to the Port Authority and the DPA
items.critical_step: Signal the bunker barge to execute an Emergency Stop immediately

items.situation: While the vessel is maneuvering in a narrow channel, the UMS alarm system indicates a 'Steering Gear Low Oil Level' for the running motor. Within seconds, the duty engineer reports a major hydraulic leak on the actuator seals. The bridge is requesting maximum rudder angles for an upcoming turn.
items.question: What do you do? Explain your actions in order.
key_steps: Immediately inform the bridge of the technical failure and steering limitation.
Change over to the standby steering gear motor and isolate the leaking unit.
Engage emergency steering procedures if remote control is lost.
Replenish the hydraulic oil reservoir to ensure the standby system remains operational.
Investigate the seal failure once the vessel is at a safe anchorage.
items.critical_step: Immediately inform the bridge of the technical failure and steering limitation.

items.situation: The vessel is scheduled to enter a designated Emission Control Area (ECA). The Second Engineer reports that the fuel changeover calculator is malfunctioning and there is uncertainty regarding the exact time required to flush the system of high-sulfur fuel. The vessel is 4 hours away from the boundary.
items.question: What do you do? Explain your actions in order.
key_steps: Calculate the manual changeover time based on fuel consumption and system volume.
Commence the changeover early to ensure the sulfur content is compliant before entry.
Document the start and end times of the changeover process in the fuel changeover log.
Verify the final sulfur content at the engine inlet using a fuel drip sample if possible.
Ensure the fuel oil service tanks are properly segregated to avoid contamination.
items.critical_step: Commence the changeover early to ensure the sulfur content is compliant before entry.

items.situation: During a black-out test required by the Class Surveyor, the Emergency Generator starts automatically but fails to connect to the emergency switchboard. The vessel is currently at anchor, and the main power has been restored, but the Surveyor insists on a successful test.
items.question: What do you do? Explain your actions in order.
key_steps: Check the operation of the air circuit breaker (ACB) and the under-voltage release coil.
Inspect the frequency and voltage output of the emergency generator to ensure they meet the synchronization criteria.
Verify the 'auto-start/auto-connect' logic settings in the Emergency Switchboard (ESB).
Rectify the fault and perform a simulated load test in the presence of the Surveyor.
Update the maintenance records to reflect the failure and the corrective actions taken.
items.critical_step: Rectify the fault and perform a simulated load test in the presence of the Surveyor.
